## GPU execution (`CUDA`, `DEVICE`) {#sec-ch14-gpu}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What**: the same code runs on a CUDA device. A block is built on the CPU and moved with `to(device)`, and the
kernels dispatch to their CUDA implementations. **Switch**: CMake `CUDA=ON`; environment `DEVICE=cuda`,
`DEVICE_ID`. **Default**: CPU. **Requires**: a CUDA build and a visible device; UCX built with CUDA for multi-GPU
runs (@sec-ch14-backends). **Order**: same scheme; round-off differs from the CPU. **Defining equation**: none.
:::

A block's tensors are created on the CPU by its constructor. The driver moves the block (`block->to(device)`) or the
whole mesh (`mesh->to(device)`) before initialising. The device is `cuda:<DEVICE_ID>`, or `cuda:<LOCAL_RANK>` when
`DEVICE_ID` is negative (@sec-ch14-launch). Torch operators run on the device. snapy's own kernels (reconstruction,
equation of state, boundaries and others) have a CPU and a CUDA implementation behind a dispatch stub
(@sec-ch01-dispatch). Collectives and decisions run on the host (@sec-ch14-collectives), so they read device values back.

### Derivation

None.

### Numerical method

The example driver `run_hydro` picks the device only if `torch::cuda::is_available()` and `DEVICE=cuda`. Otherwise it
stays on the CPU and prints nothing; "Running on CUDA" is printed only when the device is used
(`torch::cuda::is_available`, [`run_hydro.cpp:39-47`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/examples/run_hydro.cpp#L39-L47)).

The reconstruction kernels launch one CUDA block per line. A line longer than 1024 cells does not fit in one CUDA
block, so `recon_tile_width` returns a tile width instead. It starts at 256 and halves until the tile, its
stencil halo and the weights fit in 48 KiB of shared memory; the caller then runs the tiled kernel
(`recon_tile_width`, [`recon_dispatch.cu:18-46`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/recon/recon_dispatch.cu#L18-L46)).

A CUDA test of snapy runs only when snapy was built with CUDA *and* torch sees a device.
`snapy_cuda_test_enabled` returns false in a CPU build even when a GPU is visible
([`cuda_test_gate.hpp:1-15`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/cuda_test_gate.hpp#L1-L15)).

Each host read-back (`.item()`) of a device value synchronises the device. Per step, they come from the time-step
MIN, the redo flags, the signal check, the cycle-line meters and the gravity-work fixer. Issue #291 (open) measured
33 of them per step on a small 2-D moist grid with snapy 2.11.2, against 7 on 2.10.9.

seam arms from `seam_arm` [`tests/CMakeLists.txt:62-78`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/CMakeLists.txt#L62-L78). The device tolerance is `DEVICE_TOL`
([`test_vic_moist_device.py:17-20`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/test_vic_moist_device.py#L17-L20)). Pass status at the pin was not run
for this chapter.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- Issue #291 (open): on a 178 by 120 moist grid on one A100, a step cost 42.1 ms on 2.11.2 against 27.4 ms on 2.10.9
  (1.54 times). That is 3005 kernels against 2061 per step, and 33 `.item()` calls against 7. The grid is
  launch-bound, so the cost follows the kernel count. The numbers are the issue's
  ([chengcli/snapy#291](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/issues/291)) and were not re-measured here.
- A driver that asks for CUDA on a machine without it runs on the CPU silently (`run_hydro`).
:::
